title: experiment-editor-sketches-and-backlog-todo
content:
Overview:
This is a working doc for a single-page "Experiment Editor" inside Console that unifies canary, A/B experiments, and automated fallback policies. Goal is to reduce cognitive load when composing rollouts and make safe automation first-class (abort/rollback rules, verification windows, success metrics).

Audience and context:
- Primary: product console UI team + solutions engineering (helps customers create safe rollouts)
- Secondary: SREs and platform teams who map policies to on-prem/private deployments

Design goals (high level):
1) Expressiveness: allow arbitrary n-variant experiments, staged ramps, and conditional fallbacks without modal overload.
2) Safety-first defaults: short canary window + automated rollback on SLA regressions, simple guardrails visible at-a-glance.
3) Quick templates: one-click canary, A/B test, resilience test templates for common patterns.
4) Observability nearby: show per-variant metric preview and traffic traces while editing.

Primary flows (user journeys):
A. Create a simple canary (fast path)
  - User picks source model (catalog or pinned version) -> clicks "Canary" template -> sets canary size (10%) and window (30m) -> confirm -> system creates rollout with recommended abort rules and default fallback (previous stable model).
  - Acceptance: default created with minimal clicks (<= 4) and shows expected cost/latency delta estimate.

B. Compose an A/B experiment
  - User chooses n variants, uploads variant labels and optional runbook notes, sets randomization seed and allocation sliders, optionally attaches evaluation prompt set.
  - Editor shows side-by-side sample outputs, quick quality diff (token-based quality surrogate), and per-variant traffic share.
  - Acceptance: allow saving as named experiment and kick off analysis job; editable mid-run (move traffic).

C. Build an automated fallback policy
  - Drag-and-drop rule builder: metrics (latency, error_rate, accuracy proxy), operator (> / < / delta relative to baseline), duration, and action (reduce traffic, rollback, escalate).
  - Provide prebuilt policies: "SLA abort", "Safety rollback", "Gradual ramp on infra pressure".
  - Acceptance: saved policy must be human-readable sentence and testable in a dry-run mode.

Page layout (wireframe notes):
- Header: experiment title, status chip (draft/running/paused/complete), run controls (start/pause/abort)
- Left rail (compact): Experiment meta (owner, environment, pinned models), Templates (Canary / A-B / Progressive Ramp / Chaos test), History link
- Canvas (center): Variant list cards (stacked horizontally). Each card contains sample response preview, traffic slider, granularity selector (requests / sessions), and quick metrics (p95 latency, error %, cost estimate).
- Right rail: Policies & Metrics. Top: live metric preview with sparklines (per-variant). Middle: Rule Composer (drag/drop or quick add). Bottom: Audit preview + links to runbook and playbooks.
- Bottom timeline bar: shows steps (Start -> Monitor window -> Ramp -> Stable), ability to insert manual gates and define step duration. Timeline is editable; steps can be forked into sub-steps for multi-region rollouts.

Micro-interactions and defaults:
- Traffic slider offers keyboard fine-tune (arrow keys) and numeric input. Hold shift to move by 5%.
- When creating a canary default: size 10%, window 30m, abort if error_rate > 1.5x baseline OR p95 latency increases > 40% sustained for 5 minutes. These defaults are editable.
- When variant removed: warn about in-flight sessions and provide option to drain or migrate active sessions.

Policy language / UX: "SLA abort if canary.error_rate > baseline.error_rate * 1.5 for 5m -> rollback to stable" should be presented as editable sentence with tokens highlighted; click token to edit metric/operator/duration.

Quality preview: quick heuristics (not full eval) to help decide early: lexical divergence, token-length delta, stop-sequence mismatches, hallucination signal heuristics. Show confidence band and link to full eval pipeline run.

Backlog (prioritized, rough estimates):
1) Experiment Editor skeleton + header/rails (1.5 sprint) - owner: Maya
2) Variant cards + traffic slider + sample preview (1 sprint) - owner: Diego
3) Policy Composer (drag/drop + sentence UI) (2 sprints) - owner: Priya
4) Metric sparkline microservice + per-variant previews (1.5 sprint) - owner: Alexei
5) Templates library + quick create UX (0.5 sprint) - owner: Maya
6) Dry-run policy simulator (server-side) + "what-if" preview (2 sprints) - owner: Samir
7) Audit trail + manual gating UI + permission checks (1 sprint) - owner: Product Security
8) Accessibility pass + keyboard interactions (0.5 sprint) - owner: UX

Open questions / risks (to decide in grooming):
- How to surface cost estimates for long-running experiments without controlling too many variables? (linked ROLL-214)
- On private deployments, can we run metric collectors or do we require customer-provided data shippers? Need infra check with platform-engineering.
- Should experiments be mutable mid-run (move traffic) or require step-based approvals? Tradeoff between safety and agility.
- UI for multi-region forks — do we let users set independent policies per-region or prefer a template overlay?
- Data residency / telemetry privacy for sample previews in Private deployment mode.

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- Create & start a basic canary with safe defaults in <= 4 steps and see live metrics for canary vs baseline.
- Define a single rule policy and have Console enforce abort action automatically when metric crosses threshold during canary window.
- Persist experiment config to rollout service and show experiment status (running/aborted/rolled-back) in list view.

Next steps (immediate):
- Sync with infra (Alexei) on metric endpoints and what minimal metrics must be emitted for rule evaluation (ETA 2026-03-08)
- Quick proto (Figma) of center canvas + variant cards — Diego to draft by 2026-03-05
- Review default abort thresholds with SRE (Priya) and codify into template config file (ROLL-214)

Notes to reviewers:
- This doc intentionally mixes UX and product-level policy because we want the UI to reflect the policy primitives (duration, operator, baseline).
- Be pragmatic: MVP should favor a small set of well-tested policies over infinite configurability.

Related links and references:
- Existing rollout console notes (see UX-78) and canary backlog (ROLL-123)
- Example sentence-based policy editor inspiration: "Monitoring as Code" and feature-flag rule builders (links in linked_artifacts)

Scratchpad / Loose ideas (won't be implemented in MVP):
- "Dry-run sandbox" where synthetic traffic is replayed against variants to surface regressions before exposing to real users.
- Community templates market for public-safe rollout recipes.
- Integrate with Redwood Optimize to suggest quantization/model variant for cheaper A/B arms.

-- end of doc --
